newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA cattle data neutral-bearish.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA cattle data neutral-bearish.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange traders said the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly Cattle-on-Feed Report was neutral for nearby live cattle futures but bearish for deferred contracts.

The report put November large lot placements in the leading seven states at 108 percent of a year ago, toward the upper end of the 98.0- to 110.0-percent-range in a pre-report Reuter survey of analysts.
The survey had an average estimate of 105 percent.
February live cattle futures were seen opening steady to 0.10 cent a lb higher but April, 0.20 to 0.30 cent lower.
Traders noted that during the last few days there had been active interest in buying February and selling April, a trend likely to be reinforced by the USDA data.
"It confirms the spreading that has been taking place," one trader said.
USDA put the number of cattle on feed in large lots in the leading seven states at 103 percent of a year ago, relatively near the average projection in the Reuter survey of 103.2 percent.
November marketings at 97 percent were seen as mildly bullish. The average survey projection was 93.9 percent.
